params.message:
Headings end at their line in the editor; a new post opens laid out in its sections

A heading written with its text on the next line, "## Why It Matters" and the
paragraph under it without a blank line, was drawn as one large heading holding
the whole paragraph, and its raw markdown came back on focus. gentells.com reads
the same body as CommonMark: a heading line, then a paragraph. The editor now
cuts a paragraph into blocks where CommonMark does (blocksOf in piece.js), and a
paragraph left with a heading line inside it is split into the heading and its
text, so the stored paragraphs match what the site shows and the pipeline counts.

A new post opens with the sections every live post uses, in order and spelled as
on gentells.com: Signal, Why It Matters, Examples, How To Activate It with
Monday: and This quarter: under it. They are laid out by the editor over an empty
body (postLayout) and stored only once something is written under them; a
section still exactly as laid out with nothing under it is left out on save
(withoutEmptySections). An untouched post therefore stays an empty piece for
pieceStage, the empty-piece opening, autosave, the desk and the claim check, and
no empty heading reaches the site. Headings no longer count as writing in
pieceStage. Articles and decks are unchanged. The template is POST_SECTIONS in
piece.js, the one place to change the structure.
